verdict.root_cause: cart's own Redis/Valkey client calls became slow: from ~01:58:47 onward each individual cart Redis command span (HGET, HMSET, EXPIRE) sits at ~300ms of self-time, so AddItem accumulates ~900ms and the whole user-facing request ~1.2s [tr_f3ad7f93f89a]. cart's handler self-time stays sub-millisecond and no cart span carries an error status, so cart is slow-but-successful; the latency propagates up through frontend, frontend-proxy and checkout, which is why frontend-proxy's error ratio stepped up ~20x at 01:37:31 as callers hit deadlines and dropped connections [tr_f4bcda3c9058], and why frontend logged Unavailable/dial-timeout and zero-resolved-address failures against the cart endpoint during the earlier rollout churn [tr_d0d2cb41a0aa]. cart itself logs only normal info-level Valkey store operations throughout [tr_2f1a6581d4c2] and reports zero errors, with 28 intervals of no spans at all consistent with intermittent traffic gaps during the rollout [tr_36196ebbba0f]. The upstream act is the hotfix image apply at 01:35:13 and its revert at 01:45:33 [tr_87ae34783661], but the failing mechanism now is cart waiting on its backing store, not a broken artifact.
verdict.reasoning: Traces localize essentially all elapsed time to self-time inside cart's Redis command spans while sibling dependencies (product-catalog, currency, payment, flagd) stay sub-millisecond in the same traces, ruling out host-wide, collector-wide or caller-side causes [tr_f3ad7f93f89a]. The uniform ~300ms per command, independent of command type, is the signature of injected or network-level delay on the cart-to-Valkey hop rather than cart CPU or lock contention. cart returns no errors [tr_36196ebbba0f] and its logs show healthy store operations to the window's end [tr_2f1a6581d4c2], so the service is up and waiting, not crashed, partitioned or out of disk. frontend's transport-level failures and frontend-proxy's error step are downstream consequences: callers abandoning slow cart calls, plus discovery churn around the 01:35/01:45 image apply and revert [tr_d0d2cb41a0aa, tr_f4bcda3c9058, tr_87ae34783661].
open_questions: cart's latency percentiles, request rate and resource saturation were never measured; only error ratio was queried [tr_36196ebbba0f].

Valkey/Redis itself was never inspected - no metrics, logs or changes for the backing store, so whether the ~300ms originates in the store, the network hop, or a client-side delay injected by the hotfix is unsettled.

The middle ~30 minutes of both cart and frontend logs were truncated, so whether cart error-level lines exist mid-window and when frontend's transport errors actually stopped are unknown [tr_2f1a6581d4c2, tr_d0d2cb41a0aa].
The change records show one side of each image transition as unset, so what artifact cart is running now - and whether the revert fully took effect - is not established [tr_87ae34783661].

alternatives.root_cause: The revert at 01:45:33 left cart's deployment pointing at a null/unset image, so pods churned and some replicas never became ready, producing the discovery and dial failures.
alternatives.why_not: This explains the 01:36-01:46 transport errors and the traffic gaps, but not the dominant present symptom: cart pods are serving successfully with ~300ms per Redis command. A wrong or missing artifact does not produce uniformly slow, error-free store calls.

alternatives.root_cause: The hotfix image introduced a configuration value that inserts a fixed delay or a bad timeout into cart's Valkey client path, and it persisted after the revert.
alternatives.why_not: No config or flag mutations are recorded for cart - only image references [tr_87ae34783661] - and even if a setting were the origin, the mechanism the caller suffers is the wait, which classifies as dependency_latency.

proposal.expected_effect: No action proposed, so no effect is expected. The observation that would justify a later proposal is the one nobody has made yet: cart's latency percentiles (p95/p99 of the cart handler and of its Redis client spans) over the window, plus any metrics, logs or change records for the Valkey/Redis backing store. Until the ~300ms per-command self-time [tr_f3ad7f93f89a] is attributed to the store, the network hop, or client code, no permitted action targets the mechanism.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if the ~300ms is in fact held in cart's own process state (a wedged connection pool or a poisoned client config left behind by the 01:35:13 hotfix), in which case restart_service on cart would have cleared it and each further minute of delay costs checkout conversions. Evidence that would show that: cart's Redis command self-time dropping back to the sub-millisecond range seen before 01:58:47 after any unrelated container recreate, or the middle of cart's truncated log window containing client-pool error or reconnect lines. Evidence that would confirm the abstention: Valkey/Redis-side metrics showing the latency originates in the store, which no permitted action can reach.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is prolonged user-facing latency: ~1.2s requests and frontend-proxy's ~9.3% error ratio [tr_f4bcda3c9058] continue until a human acts. The risk of the action I am declining — restart_service on cart, the class the synthesizer named — is why I decline it: restart_service requires evidence pointing at process state rather than at a change, and the evidence points the other way. cart's handler self-time is sub-millisecond, it logs only normal info-level Valkey operations [tr_2f1a6581d4c2], it reports zero errors [tr_36196ebbba0f], and all the latency sits inside Redis command spans [tr_f3ad7f93f89a] — that is a dependency, not a wedged process. A restart would discard cart's in-process cache, drop in-flight carts, and return the same ~300ms per command against the same backing store, while destroying the current container as a diagnostic artifact — relevant because the change records leave one side of each image transition unset, so what cart is actually running now is unestablished [tr_87ae34783661]. rollback_image is likewise unavailable in practice: its precondition is a recorded prior image tag, and the change log records 'None' rather than a concrete tag on both transitions [tr_87ae34783661]. revert_config is excluded outright — cart's change history contains only image-reference changes, no config or flag mutations [tr_87ae34783661]. The action that fits the mechanism, restore_store against the Valkey backing store, is marked unavailable, and the store is not in the blast radius as a legal target.
proposal.blast_radius: Nobody sees a change, because nothing changes. The services currently absorbing the fault continue to: frontend and checkout as cart's direct callers, frontend-proxy and load-generator above them. The restart I am declining would have hit cart alone for the duration of the recreate, with frontend and checkout seeing connection resets on their inbound edges — the same hop that already logged dial timeouts and zero-resolved-address failures during the earlier rollout churn [tr_d0d2cb41a0aa], meaning a recreate risks re-triggering the discovery gap that produced frontend-proxy's error step.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Five services alerted simultaneously across the cart/frontend/checkout path, which is broader than a single-service latency warning and cannot be dismissed. No open incident to attribute it to, and the alert pattern doesn't single out a cause - cart+flagd or a shared downstream are both plausible.
